subject: Some questions relating to timeShiftImages / recordTable

messages.subject: Some questions relating to timeShiftImages / recordTable
parts:
Hello, 

I am new to the camtrapR package and I am currently familiarising myself with the tool. 
First of all, thanks very much for this wonderful package!!! And thanks a lot for the vignettes that are very well written and easy to follow.

I however have some questions... Four precisely:

Q1: In relation to the 'timeShiftImages' function.
I have double camera stations and therefore the directories are organised as such: Station > Camera.
Following the steps in the provided vignette, the time shift is defined for a station (or a camera in a station). But what if the time shift should not apply to all the photographs found in the camera folder? (e.g. I  checked my camera several times to change the batteries and only between the second and third download did I set the time or date wrong). Is there a way to apply a more subtle timeshift?

Q2: In relation to the 'recordTable' function.
The photos for which no species tag was defined in digikam were not get extracted. Would it be possible to extract all data and leave a blank cell under the species column attribute, if no tag was defined?

R code:
rec.db <- recordTable(inDir          = wd_renamed_timeshift_copy,
                      IDfrom         = "metadata",
                      cameraID       = "filename",
                      camerasIndependent = FALSE,
                      #exclude            = c(),
                      #minDeltaTime        = 60,
                      #deltaTimeComparedTo = 
                      timeZone = "UTC",
                      #stationCol = "Station",
                      writecsv = TRUE,
                      outDir = wd_data,
                      metadataHierarchyDelimitor = "|",
                      metadataSpeciesTag = "species",
                      #additionalMetadataTags = c("EXIF:num.ind", "EXIF:age"),
                      removeDuplicateRecords = FALSE 
                      )

R warning message:
StationA : 639 images
Warning: StationA :  removed 636 records out of 639 because of missing species metadata tag
StationB : 615 images
Warning: StationB :  removed 614 records out of 615 because of missing species metadata tag
StationC : 623 images
Warning: StationC :  removed 621 records out of 623 because of missing species metadata tag

Q3:  In relation to the 'recordTable' function.
#minDeltaTime and #deltaTimeComparedTo allow me to define the dependence/independence of the records. Would it be possible to have an attribute column in the exported csv file that says whether the record is considered to be dependent, without removing it? 

Q4: In relation to the 'recordTable/recordTableIndividual' functions
Is it possible to define the csv file names? I would like to use this function in a loop and it seems to overwrite it. 

I look forward to hearing from you.
Kind regards, 

Elsa

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Some questions relating to timeShiftImages / recordTable
parts:
Dear Elsa,
I apologise for the late reply to your questions. Here is your reply:

Q1: Currently there is no built-in function to change date and time of only selected pictures in a camera folder. What you could do instead is admittedly troublesome. Move only the images you want to shift in another temporary camera directory. Adjust the camera column in the time shift table accordingly and run. Move the images back in the camera directory. It is a quick and dirty fix, but not a good solution.

Q2: Likewise, currently this is not implemented. It is a good idea though for one of the next releases.

Q3: This would be possible, but is currently not implemented, sorry. It would be a new arguments somewhat similar to the argument removeDuplicateRecords in allowing you to keep or remove unnecessary records. I will try to implement it soon.

Q4: Also, currently the file name is fixed. For now it would be easiest if you do as you suggested in your second post, save the tables as data.frames and save afterwards. Also a good idea to allow the user to specify an alternative file name. 

I am sorry none of the features you ask is currently implemented. I will take it all into consideration for the next release.
Thank you for using camtrapR and thank you for your helpful suggestions to improve it!

Best regards,
Jürgen
